messages:
amanda: FYI - running a short POC for a Singapore financial client. They need a small pack for vendor risk: data-flow diagram, short subprocessor list (with where backups live), and SIG/CAIQ excerpts for crypto/network controls. Can we pull together by EOD?

leo: Hosted POC in asia-southeast1, right? Quick heads-up: we replicate backups to a DR region by default unless we opt-out. Need to know if customer allows cross-region backups (we can set backup-region to asia-southeast1 only for POC).

priya: Correct, hosted in SG. Customer legal insists on no cross-border backups during POC. They asked for an explicit field in the CSV: backup_region and backup_retention_days.

amanda: Understood. Can ops confirm we can pin backups to asia-southeast1 for the POC window and set retention to 7 days? Also they want the SIG-high-level answers for controls: e.g., network segregation, TLS, key management.

leo: Ops note: we can disable cross-region replication for the POC bucket and set retention to 7 days. However, some telemetry (health metrics) by default flow to our central observability cluster; we can route POC metrics to a regional metrics endpoint and keep only aggregated counters.

legal-bot: legal: recommend a POC addendum: (1) subprocessor restriction to SG/SEA, (2) 7-day log retention, (3) prohibition on human inspection of raw requests without written consent. I can draft.

priya: They also asked 'who has potential access to unredacted payloads' and 'are backups encrypted with a key we control?'.

leo: Access: support/ops don't access request payloads in normal ops. We redact sensitive fields at ingestion for hosted customers. For extra assurance we can enable request-payload redaction and enable audit logging for any support access (requires ticket/approval). Encryption: backups are AES-256 at rest and wrapped with KMS. We can offer customer-managed keys for Private deployments, but not for Hosted POC.

amanda: Ok — include a clear sentence about no routine human access and audit trail requirement. Also provide the CAIQ snippets for SC-8 (transmission security) and SC-13 (encryption).

presales-bot: presales: bundle prepared -> https://redwood.internal/presales/sg-fin-poc (files: flow-diagram-apac.pdf, subprocessor-list-backups.csv, caiq-snippets-enc-net.md) :file_folder:

leo: I'll paste a tiny inline ASCII flow you can reuse in their packet:

``
App (SG customer infra) -> TLS -> Edge (asia-southeast1) -> Inference service (asia-southeast1)
                              -> Optional KV cache (asia-southeast1)
Artifacts/backups -> GCS bucket (asia-southeast1, replication disabled for POC)
Metrics (aggregated) -> Regional metrics endpoint (asia-southeast1)
Audit logs -> Central audit store (access restricted; copies not included for POC)
``

priya: CSV note: subprocessor rows include: vendor_name, role, primary_region, backup_region, backup_encrypted(Y/N), vendor_socs_link. Make backup_region explicit.

amanda: Great. Can we add a short note in the CSV that backup_region override is POC-limited and will be reverted after POC end date? Also need a one-paragraph DPA addendum from legal.

legal-bot: Drafted addendum and attached to the bundle (dpa-poc-addendum.pdf). It contains the POC window, subprocessor-region restriction, 7-day retention, and no-PII access without consent.

priya: One more ask from the client — a CAIQ-style line: "How do you protect data in transit and at rest?" Can we give a very short plain-English answer referencing TLS 1.2+/AES-256/KMS and link to the CAIQ excerpt.

leo: I'll excerpt CAIQ items plus provide the plain-English blurb. Will also include SOC2 + ISO links for the top subprocessors.

amanda: Timeline: bundle out by 17:00 SGT?

leo: Affirmative. I'll add a signed subprocessor manifest (checkbox for backup_region pinned to asia-southeast1) and a short ops attestation note.

presales-bot: upload complete -> https://redwood.internal/presales/sg-fin-poc/bundle-1802004321.zip :file_folder:

amanda: Perfect, thanks all :rocket: I'll send to their counsel and loop back here with any follow-ups.
